summary:
Visual QA, round 5. Not a pass: 5 UI blockers, all small. No screen is broken, but each is below the Linear, Stripe, Vercel bar.

What I did
- Built 15 fresh accounts through the real screens, one per billing state. Added a team (owner, admin, member) whose trial ended, a person who signed up with no password, and a person with no organization.
- Took 946 screenshots at 1440, 768 and 390 in light and dark, and looked at them on contact sheets and at full size where something looked off.
- Covered signup, the picker, verify email, welcome, launcher, every billing tab in every state, test checkout, invoices, cancel and pause, seat and warehouse limits, My account, the "another organization" page, banners and lock screens in all four apps, view only dialogs, pricing and the get started wizard, the email templates, and billing off on the production mode portal (3310).
- Measured focus order, focus rings, hover and pressed colors, reduced motion, a slow network, contrast, and sideways scroll at 360 and 320.

Round 4 visual blockers: all fixed
- The confirm change dialog gives focus back to "Review change" after Esc.
- Invoices at 768 keep date, number and amount on one line.
- The phone setup guide says "Show the other 4 steps" and its quiet links start under the step title.
- On signup the code choice is its own underlined row under the button, and a company name password says why.
- The code sign in step has its own address, survives a reload, and uses the Test mode pill.
- Member rows use the design system select.

Clean this round
- No sideways scroll from 320 to 1440. No contrast failure (one false alarm on the pricing hero).
- A focus ring on every control. Confetti is off under reduced motion.
- Banner buttons in WMS, Pulse and CRM are full strength and land on the Portal in one press.
- An admin's banner names who to ask and has no pay button.

Seen but not counted as blockers
- The view only WMS dashboard threw one hydration error ("server rendered text didn't match the client") in about 19 loads, on a first load while memory was short. 0 of 13 after that, also with a slowed CPU.
- The portal dev server was killed for memory once during my run (20:08 UTC). It came back with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0 and I took the failed shots again. I did not restart it myself.
- Real Stripe is still not run. That is outside what I can see.

I changed no product code and wrote no file outside the scratch folder. All 7 services are up, rate limit counters are cleared, no account is locked. About 110 throwaway `vqa-...@kitstak-e2e.example` users from rounds 4 and 5 are left in the local database.

Screenshots, sheets, scripts and logs: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/visual5/ (notes in notes.txt, sheets in sheets/, scripts in scripts/).

- Words: this page says "Not confirmed" and "Confirm my email". The banner right above it says "Enter the 6 digit code we emailed you", and Billing says "Verify your email first". Two words for one thing.

summary:
OPERATIONAL QA, ROUND 5: not a pass. 6 blockers (3 backend, 3 ui). None is on the money path. Every charge, credit, access row and email I checked was right to the cent.

**How I tested**
- Real Chromium plus signed webhook calls and direct API calls on the shared dev stack, test gateway on, plan gate on in all six processes. Also the production build with no keys on port 3310.
- About 15 new organizations and 9 invited people, made through the real screens.
- After each step I read `core.entitlements`, `billing_subscriptions`, `billing_invoices`, `billing_events`, `billing_emails` and the audit log.
- No product code edited. Tree is clean. Scripts, outputs and screenshots are in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/opqa5/`.

**What held**
- **Signup:** wizard handoff with prefilled fields and $395.20 hero, bad inputs, weak passwords, duplicate email (also in capitals with spaces), tampered cart clamped to catalog limits, script tags in the company name, refresh and Back, double click (one trial, one welcome mail), verify code and "Change email".
- **Trial:** each app opens. The 7, 3 and 1 day mails and the "trial ended" mail went out. Add and remove apps in trial worked. Trial end with no card gave view only.
- **Checkout:** success, declined, not enough money, bank approval pass and fail, promo TEST10, expired date, Back, two sessions (the older one closes), and a tab closed after paying (the plan still applied).
- **Plan changes:** seats, warehouses, apps, monthly to yearly and back. I checked every amount by hand, for example $11.60, $10.83 credit, $139.60, $1,153.46 and $1,329.95 credit. Four confirms fired at once made one invoice.
- **Webhooks:** replay answers `duplicate`, stale and lying events change nothing, six bad signatures get 400 with no row, other organizations are untouched. Ledger: 4,012 processed, 14 ignored, 0 failed.
- **Late payment:** past due, three retry mails, last day mail, view only on day 8, card update back to active with receipt. An automatic retry also recovered a plan by itself.
- **Cancel and pause:** cancel, keep, reactivate, cancel with a bill open (bill voided, nothing charged later), pause, undo, start again, cancel during a trial with a card (no charge).
- **People:** invites, seat counts, seat offer ($24.05, declined then paid), seat limit through the Portal and CRM APIs, remove, leave, guest and billing-only roles.
- **Roles:** member, admin and another organization's owner are refused on all six billing actions with no database change. Deleting an organization with a live plan is refused.
- **Production build:** 0 console messages, pay buttons off with the honest line, test routes 404, job and Stripe webhook answer 503.

**Round 4 blockers, rechecked: all fixed**
- WMS no longer reloads for a person with no organization.
- Email and banner links carry the organization and open the right one for a person in two.
- An old session is signed out in every app right after a password reset.
- A refresh on the code sign in step keeps the step.
- Code sign in works a second time.
- The banner button in Pulse and CRM works in one click and is not dimmed.
- An admin who cannot pay reads "Ask Kim Vale to update the card" with no button.

**Not covered this round**
- All four apps in one trial with the trial banner: the run crashed at the WMS, so I only saw each app under trial one by one.
- The admin banner in the view only state: the retry paid before I could look.
- The two-tab checkout race: I ran the lighter concurrent-confirm test instead.

**Things I disturbed and put back**
- The portal dev server was killed by the memory limit twice. I restarted it both times with `ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0`.
- My rate limit test locked the seeded `maya@northwind-robotics.example`. I cleared the lock and she signs in again (200).
- All seven services are up and no account is locked. My test organizations remain in the local database.

blockers.title: A warehouse admin can make a verified KitStak account for any free address, take an owner's billing invite with it, and keep a password on a stranger's account
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/server/auth/credentials.ts (upsertCoreIdentity writes emailVerified: true), apps/wms/src/server/repositories/users.ts (createUser, and the admin password reset for an identity 'managed here'), packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts (requireProvenMailbox trusts email_verified), POST /api/users and POST /api/tenancy/warehouse in the WMS
blockers.detail:
WHAT IS WRONG. Round 4 made email_verified the proof that a person owns an invited mailbox. The WMS 'Add user' screen makes a core.user row for any address that has no account yet, with a password the warehouse admin types, and marks it verified. No email goes to that address. On this branch anyone can become a warehouse admin: sign up (no email code needed), make an organization, start the free trial with WMS (no card), set up a warehouse. So the round 4 invite takeover is open again, and a second hole comes with it.

REPRODUCED on the dev stack, real HTTP calls, throwaway accounts removed afterwards.

(a) Invite takeover. Run: node docs/billing/.review/sec5/wms-verified-takeover.mjs. Real output: '1. the owner invites a bookkeeper with the billing role: 200' / '2. the ADMIN reads the open invite: 200 id 09bdb73b... role billing' / '3. the admin makes an organization of their own: 200 | the admin email is verified: false' / 'free trial with WMS: trial' / '4. sets up a warehouse in the WMS: 200' / '5. WMS "Add user" with the invited address and a password the admin typed: 201' / 'that account in core.user: email_verified true' / '6. signs in at the Portal as the invited address: 200' / '7. accepts the owner's billing invite: 200' / 'roles in the victim organization now: owner, admin, bookkeeper address = billing' / '8. /billing/cancel 200, the billing team page lists "Not Bookkeeper"'. The admin now holds a billing manager account of the victim organization and can cancel or pause the plan, change billing details and open the card page. SPEC P15 says only an owner can add a billing manager. (The one step not done over HTTP is 'Start free trial': the probe calls startTrial, the same package function the Portal button calls.)

(b) Account pre hijack. Run: node docs/billing/.review/sec5/wms-prehijack.mjs. Real output: an unverified person with a free WMS trial adds a 'user' with a victim address: 201, account email_verified true, 'emails sent to the victim: []'. The victim later signs in with 'Email me a code instead' and lands on '/', with 'no word about a password'. 'password rows of the account now: has_password true'. '3. the attacker signs in as the victim with the password they typed in the WMS: 200'. For an account made by plain signup Better Auth removes the unproven password at the first code sign in (round 4 probe prehijack.mjs). That protection only runs for an unverified account, so marking it verified switches it off. While the account is only in the attacker's organization the WMS also lets the attacker set a new password for it at any time.

SCOPE. emailVerified: true in upsertCoreIdentity is older than this branch, but before this branch a WMS needed a manual grant from KitStak. The self serve trial, sign in by code, and the round 4 rule that trusts email_verified are all new here.

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE. An account that someone else made for an address is born unverified. Only the mailbox can prove the mailbox: the emailed code, the proof in the Portal invite link, or the WMS welcome link. At the first proof, any password the mailbox owner did not set and every session are removed, and the person is told in one sentence (the same rule the Portal already has for 'password_removed'). After the owner has proven the mailbox, or once the account is in any other organization, no warehouse admin can set or reset its password. Decide what happens to WMS made accounts that exist today and write it in GO-LIVE.md. Tests: a unit test that upsertCoreIdentity makes a new identity with email_verified false; a shared layer test that an account made by WMS 'Add user' is refused at accept-invitation with INVITE_NEEDS_PROVEN_MAILBOX; a browser test of (b) that ends with the attacker's password answering 401; the WMS invited user can still get in through the welcome link.

blockers.title: A stranger can lock any 'no password' account out of KitStak for a day with 20 requests, again every day, and the screen still says a code is on its way
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/server/auth.ts guardEmailCodes (keys billing:code:<email>, billing:code-day:<email>, billing:code-signin:<email>, billing:code-signin-day:<email>), apps/portal/src/server/signup-actions.ts (requestSignInCodeAction, requestPasswordResetAction), packages/billing/src/server/rate-limit.ts
blockers.detail:
WHAT IS WRONG. One budget per address (5 per 10 minutes, 20 per day) covers verify codes, reset codes and sign in codes, and every anonymous request for that address counts. An account made with 'Email me a code instead' has no password row at all since round 4, so an emailed code is its only way in. A person with no account and no session can use the whole budget. Round 4 listed this as worth fixing; it is unchanged, and code only accounts are now a first class path, so it is a lockout of the account owner, not only a nuisance.

REPRODUCED. Run: node docs/billing/.review/sec5/code-budget-lockout.mjs. Real output: '1. the victim: verified, password rows: 0' / '2. 24 anonymous reset requests for the victim address answered: 200 x20 then 429 429 429 429 (831 ms)' / 'counters: billing:code-day count 24' / 'emails the victim got from this: 20' / 'one more request now: 429 We sent many codes to this address today. Try again tomorrow.' / '3. the victim asks for a sign in code. The screen says: "If ... has a KitStak account, a code is on its way. It works for 10 minutes."' / 'sign in codes mailed to the victim in the next 12 seconds: 0' / '4. "Forgot password" for the victim. Reset codes mailed in the next 10 seconds: 0'. The probe cleared the short 10 minute counter to stand in for waiting; a real attacker needs about 40 minutes of patience or four addresses, once a day. The day window starts at the first request and refused requests keep counting, so 20 requests a day keep the door shut for good. By reading the code, the sign in try counters (10 per 10 minutes, 30 per day per address, right or wrong) can be used up the same way with wrong codes.

Impact: the only owner of an organization can be kept out of the Portal while a late payment runs to view only. The victim also gets 20 code emails, and is then told a code is on its way when none is sent (SPEC rule: never invent success).

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE. A stranger can never stop the owner of a mailbox from getting in. The limit that protects the mailbox from spam slows sends for one address (for example one email per minute, then one per 10 minutes) and never becomes a wall for a day. The limit that protects the 6 digit code from guessing stays on the code itself (5 tries per code) and on the caller, not on a counter any anonymous caller can fill for someone else. A browser that signed in to this account before (a signed device cookie) keeps its own small budget. When no code was sent because of a limit, the screen says so with the real wait; the same sentence is shown for an address with no account, so nothing leaks. Tests: 30 anonymous requests for an address, then the owner asks for a sign in code and a reset code and both arrive within the stated wait; the same with 30 wrong sign in codes.

blockers.title: A person invited from the CRM can no longer join, and is told to open an invite email that was never sent
blockers.where: apps/crm/src/server/services/members.ts createInvitation (POST /api/v1/invitations writes core.invitation itself, no email), apps/crm/src/features/wizards/invite-accept.tsx and model/invites.ts inviteLink (/welcome/invite/<id>), packages/billing/src/server/auth-hooks.ts requireProvenMailbox, apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/invite/[invitationId] (bare link with no proof)
blockers.detail:
WHAT IS WRONG. The round 4 rule 'accepting an invite needs email_verified' holds at every app. The Portal invite email carries a proof that marks the address verified. The CRM 'Invite members' dialog does not use that door: it writes the invitation row itself and gives the inviter a link to copy. No email is sent, so there is no proof. A new person who opens that link makes an account on the CRM signup page (the CRM has no email codes), presses Join, and is refused. Accounts made before email codes existed are unverified too, so existing customers hit the same wall. The message points at an email that does not exist, and nothing offers a way to prove the mailbox.

REPRODUCED. Run: node docs/billing/.review/sec5/crm-invite-join.mjs. Real output: '3. the same invite through the CRM "Invite members" API: 201' / 'emails to the invited person: []' / '4. the new hire opens the copied link, signed out: 307 /login?next=/welcome/invite/<id>' / 'makes an account on the CRM signup page: 200' / '5. presses "Join": 403 INVITE_NEEDS_PROVEN_MAILBOX "Open the link in your invite email to join. That shows the email is yours."' / 'members of the organization now: owner only' / 'emails the new hire has to act on: []'. The same probe shows the CRM door skips the shared invite rules: an owner with an unverified email is refused at the shared API (403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED) and accepted by the CRM API (201), and the day counter for invites is not touched. That part is low risk today only because the CRM sends no mail.

The integrator's own notes fit this: the CRM wizards spec stopped at step 2 and 7 tests after it did not run, and 'Invite page without the emailed proof: not done'.

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE. One invite door. The CRM dialog calls the shared createInvitation, so the verified inviter rule, the day cap, the seat hold and the invite email with its proof all apply, and the invited person joins from the email with one click. A link opened without the proof, in the Portal or the CRM, never shows a form that will be refused. It says in one sentence that the address must be confirmed and offers 'Email me a code' for the invited address on that same screen; the code proves the mailbox and the join goes through. 'Copy link' never carries the proof, because the inviter can read it. Tests: a browser test in the CRM suite where an owner invites a new address, the person joins from the email; a second where the person opens a bare link, confirms with a code and joins; the CRM wizards spec runs to the end.

summary:
Not a pass. Three backend blockers, each reproduced on the running dev stack with throwaway accounts that were removed afterwards. Probe scripts are in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec5/ (ignored by git): wms-verified-takeover.mjs, wms-prehijack.mjs, code-budget-lockout.mjs, crm-invite-join.mjs, plus blocked.mjs and verified-flag.mjs for the rechecks. I edited no product code and restarted no server. The working tree is clean.

ROUND 4 BLOCKERS, RECHECKED
- Blocker 1 (code sign in worked once): fixed. sec4/lockout.mjs now prints 'a second sign in code was mailed: yes' and lands on /settings/account with the password notice.
- Blocker 2 (switched off person comes back with Forgot password): fixed with a real fact row. sec5/blocked.mjs puts a row in core.sign_in_blocks and tries every door: password sign in 401, reset request 200 with no email, sign in code not mailed, a reset code obtained before the block answers INVALID_OTP (also with a trailing slash), no new session. Note: the old sec4/deactivated-reset.mjs still 'succeeds' because it switches a person off the old way (deleting the password row), which no longer means switched off.
- Blocker 3 (admin takes a billing invite): closed for the signup path (403 INVITE_NEEDS_PROVEN_MAILBOX), but open again through the WMS 'Add user' screen. That is blocker 1 of this round. The fix also broke joining from a CRM invite. That is blocker 3.
- Round 3 billing role rule: still holds (sec4/billing-role.mjs, all 403).

CHECKED AND SOUND THIS ROUND
- Production mode portal with no keys (port 3310): /test-gateway pages 404, /dev/outbox 404, test webhook 404, Stripe webhook 503, job tick 503. Dev: unsigned test webhook 400.
- Webhooks: signature on the raw body first, ledger row and state change in one transaction, state read fresh from the gateway, concurrent duplicates resolved by the ledger insert.
- No price, amount or proration date from the browser. Catalog cents recomputed by hand: every yearly and bundle amount is a whole cent.
- Redirects: 15 hostile next and org values against /org/switch, the Portal login and the four app logins all land on a same origin or trusted address.
- email_verified cannot be self set: sign up and update-user with emailVerified true leave it false at the Portal and the CRM; change-email is disabled; signup is closed at WMS, Projects and Pulse.
- Invoices, PDFs and the activity export are scoped to the session's organization. Email HTML is escaped.
- packages/billing: 30 files, 572 tests passed, 1 skipped, run by me with the database up. No key shaped string in the tree. Migrations 0007 to 0011 and WMS 0013 are additive and safe to run again.

NOT BLOCKERS, WORTH FIXING
1. Real Stripe has still never been run. The adapter is only checked against SDK types and a mocked SDK (pending updates with always_invoice, a future proration date, credit notes on a refund are all unproven). This stays the largest open risk and the integrator says so plainly.
2. PRICING_IS_PLACEHOLDER is false and its comment cites docs/billing/DECISIONS.md section 1 (an owner decision dated 2026-11-23, recorded by the orchestrating session). The standing brief for this effort still says only the Pulse price is owner confirmed. The code is honest about its source, but the owner should confirm the CRM, WMS and Projects prices in writing before go live.
3. /org/switch changes the active organization on a GET. A link on another site can flip a signed in person to another of their own organizations. Membership is checked and every action still compares the rendered organization, so the risk is low.
4. Sign in by code tells accounts apart after 5 wrong tries ('Too many tries with that code' only for a real account with a live code). Accepted risk A1 already covers signup, so this is minor.
5. Cancel, pause and undo still write the plan row without the organization lock the webhooks take. The gateway's own event and the reconcile job heal it.
6. A first payment left 'incomplete' that then expires would be stored as an ended plan. Check against real Stripe.
7. Database tests still skip silently when Postgres is not reachable.
8. The invite and org names go into email text as typed. They are HTML escaped, but a name that is a web address becomes a link in most mail apps.

CRITIC, ROUND 5: not a pass. Scorecard 25 of 30 with no zero. This is the first round over the bar of 24 (rounds 1 to 4: 20, 22, 23, 23). Six blockers remain: one needs the owner's Stripe keys, five are small. Full scorecard: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/reviews/critic-round-5.md. Scripts, output and screenshots: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/critic5/ (not committed).

NOTE ON THE REQUEST: the relayed user request was the single word "Status". I did the review step the workflow assigned.

HOW I TESTED
- Real Chromium (Playwright) on the shared dev stack with the plan gate on, plus the production build with no keys on port 3310. I looked at the screenshots.
- Four people made by signup or invite: a password buyer at 1280 light (CRM and WMS, 5 seats), a code only buyer at 360 dark (Pulse), an invited teammate, and a buyer on the production build.
- Every payment used the test gateway. No Google or Microsoft buttons were on screen (no keys).
- I did not walk the bookkeeper path again. Line 13 keeps its round 4 score.
- I did not edit product code, restart a server or reset rate limits. My test accounts (Cedar Point Supply, Tidewater Crating, Lakeshore Fixtures) are still in the local database.

ROUND 4 BLOCKERS: 4 OF 5 CLOSED, EACH CHECKED IN THE BROWSER
- WMS and Pulse banner button: now full strength, and one click lands on the Portal from the WMS, Pulse and CRM.
- One front door: sign in and forgot password on the other apps all go to the Portal. A signed out Pulse deep link, a code, and I landed on that exact page. A reload on the code step kept the field and sent no second email. My account exists and offers "Set a password".
- Company name in a password: now says "Do not use your company name in your password." under the field.
- Invite emails: marked sent at once.
- Still open: real Stripe.

SCORE MOVEMENT
- Card failure went 1 to 2. One account for the suite went 1 to 2.
- Still 1: time to value and things asked (Google sign in unseen), checkout (real Stripe unseen), seat fairness (Slack gives credit unasked), reading level.

MEASURED
- Signup to picker: 0.6 s with a password. Code path on a phone, product link to launcher: 3 fields, 4 clicks, 6.1 s.
- First WMS screen: 2 clicks, 2.9 s.
- $395.20 matched on the pricing page, signup panel, picker, pay page, billing home and invoice. The seat, promo, yearly and add an app amounts I checked by hand were right.
- Late payment fixed and the WMS open again 3.8 s after saving a good card.
- Production with no keys: "Billing is not available right now. Nothing will be charged." and the pay button is off.

BLOCKERS
1. Real Stripe has never run (backend, needs the owner's test keys).
2. A teammate must make a password to join. The invite page has no code door (backend).
3. Every sign in that returns to another app logs three console errors (ui).
4. Three wrong turns on the money path: "Update card" needs a second click, the first payment forgets the app I came from, and one plan change sentence is long and wrong (ui).
5. A member is told "Ask Dana Whitfield" with no way to ask, and "See Billing" leads to the same sentence (ui).
6. The signup page makes me feel safe, not eager (ui).

VERDICT IN ONE LINE: the billing side is better than the Stripe portal, Slack and Vercel. Signup ties Linear. I am impressed, but not wowed from the first screen to the last, and nobody has seen a real Stripe charge.
